conditionality: The gain is rated slight because no unit states how large the carbon removal is per hectare or per year: the zaï figure is an organic-matter content change cited second-hand from an earlier study, the Burkina Faso farm comparison is a soil-fertility test against a single control farm, and the Loess Plateau statement is a review citation [ev_soil_organic_carbon_kabo04_1, ev_soil_organic_carbon_sawa11h1_3, ev_carbon_sequestration_luca21_1]. effect_mechanism: Micro-catchment structures (fish-scale pits, micro-basins, trenches) concentrate scarce rainfall around planted trees or vegetation, building up soil carbon and biomass. A meta-analysis of Chinese studies found fish-scale pits raised soil organic carbon storage on the Loess Plateau by 79.86% over 11 to 30 years, with terracing raising it by 14.11% to 60.96% over the same period [ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_12].
conditionality: This benefit does not guarantee tree establishment. In an Ethiopian on-farm trial, micro-basins and trenches around newly planted tree seedlings showed no significant difference in survival compared with untreated control seedlings across three tree species; the authors attributed this null result to dry-season moisture scarcity too severe for the structures to bridge, together with insect and termite attack and browsing by free-grazing livestock [ev_establishment_survival_kinuthia20_1]. The evidence base is thin, three sources across Burkina Faso, China and Ethiopia, so this picture rests on a small, specific set of measurements rather than a broad literature.

effect_mechanism: Check dams and percolation tanks raise catchment water yield by detaining monsoon runoff so it infiltrates to the aquifer rather than running off downstream. In Rajasthan, India, check dams, measured against no-dam conditions (the runoff otherwise flowing on down the ephemeral stream), added recharge of 33 mm over their combined catchment in an average year and 17 mm in a year the authors called 'dry' [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_dash17_1, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_dash17_2]. In Andhra Pradesh, a small percolation tank — managed aquifer recharge (MAR) by an earth weir across an intermittent stream — sent 57 to 63 percent (average 61 percent) of its stored water to the hard-rock aquifer rather than losing it to evapotranspiration [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_mass14_1], and tank percolation supplied 40 percent of the water pumped from nearby irrigation boreholes in both a rainfall-deficit year [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_mass14_2] and a normal-rainfall year, when it reached seven additional boreholes [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_mass14_3].
conditionality: Both dam figures are measured recharge added by the structure, with no-dam conditions used only as the counterfactual, not an actually measured case; the authors put 'dry' in quotation marks, since mean rainfall was similar in both years and the real difference was rainfall intensity and dry-spell length rather than a named drought [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_dash17_1, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_dash17_2]. The percolation-tank figures come from one tank at one site; most of the percolated water is drawn back by boreholes close to the tank, so the recharge benefit is local, and the paper itself flags its percolation-efficiency estimate as in the high range of earlier regional estimates [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_mass14_1]. The borehole-contribution shares rest on an electrical-conductivity mixing analysis built on stated assumptions about tank-water and aquifer-water conductivity [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_mass14_2, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_mass14_3]. All five units are irrigated cropping systems in India; the mechanism is not yet shown for rainfed systems.

effect_mechanism: Watershed-scale soil and water conservation is reported to raise groundwater, used here as a component of catchment water yield: stone bunds, zaï and half-moons applied at watershed scale increase ground water level [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_zoug14_1]; in Burkina Faso improved well levels are linked to SWC measures that control surface runoff and improve infiltration [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_kabo04_1]; ISRO survey data record an increase in groundwater recharge in treated areas in India [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_iegind11_3]; piezometers recorded groundwater levels rising in 16 of 21 non-desert districts with an average increase of 1.42 meters [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_verm19_3]; the Uttarakhand water budget shows aquifer recharge up 3.3 percent and water yield from catchment areas up 4.9 percent [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_utk22_5]; and in Ethiopia improvements in the water table made small-scale irrigation possible [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_eth16_7]. In Burkina Faso, cited studies show soil and water conservation techniques improving the availability of ground water in many villages, especially large rock bunds known as digues filtrantes [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_sawa11h1_6]. In Ethiopia's Mendae catchment a water balance gave groundwater recharge of 107.7 mm after water harvesting against 8 mm before (Negusse et al., 2013, cited by Gebremeskel et al.) [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_gebr18_11]. On the other side, the same capture reduces what leaves the catchment: water outflows from treated catchments have been found halved compared with untreated catchments (Garg et al., 2012; Gates et al., 2011, cited by Gebremeskel et al.), reviews cite a decrease in runoff generation harming downstream social–ecological systems (Batchelor et al., 2003; Glendenning and Vervoort, 2011; Garg et al., 2012, cited by Dile et al.), and a global model suggested rainwater harvesting would reduce annual river flows by 18% on average and by up to 80% in a single basin (Wisser et al., 2010, cited by Glendenning et al.) [ev_water_yield_gebr18_9, ev_water_yield_dile13_9, ev_water_yield_glen12_10]. A landscape review of rainwater harvesting across African drylands also lists groundwater recharge and the filling of wells among its benefits [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_vohl09_3]. A CILSS regional synthesis adds a further recharge observation: in Batodi, Niger, the water level in village wells rose by about 14 metres between 1994 and 2004, which the villagers attributed to the runoff-harvesting works [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_botreij09_18].
conditionality: This row is for downstream users and basin planners: it asks what capturing water upstream does to the water that reaches streams and reservoirs below, not whether the farm that captures it has more. Studies disagree because the recharge side counts water entering the ground near treated land, while the outflow side counts water leaving the catchment, and the same works can raise the first and lower the second [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_utk22_5, ev_water_yield_gebr18_9]. Scale and intensity also separate them: the outflow losses come from large-scale implementation and basin-wide models, while other studies find limited or no downstream impact on stream flows from small-scale storage, even when implemented widely (Schreider et al., 2002; De Winnaar and Jewitt, 2010; Andersson et al., 2011) [ev_water_yield_dile13_10, ev_water_yield_rock10_1]. The recharge gains have limits in their own sources: without data from untreated sites the Indian project impact is unclear [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_iegind11_3], subsidised tube-well pumping has possibly wiped out any increases in recharge [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_iegind11_4], and in Burkina Faso the number of wells with water year round has not increased significantly [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_kabo04_2]. The Uttarakhand figures are a modelled water budget [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_utk22_5], the outflow findings are all cited second-hand, and most other units are programme reports or cited statements; the digues filtrantes finding is cited from another study, with no figures [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_sawa11h1_6]. That listing is the review's own qualitative evaluation across cited sources, not a measured recharge figure [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_vohl09_3]. That well-level rise is the villagers' own attribution rather than a measurement against a comparable untreated well, and it adds to the recharge side of this row rather than resolving the conflict with the downstream-outflow evidence [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_botreij09_18].

Sand dams in Burkina Faso and Kenya are similarly credited with recharging groundwater and supplying wells for domestic use and irrigation [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_foxr03_8, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_biaz12_27], and sand dams more generally can raise local groundwater, though the extent of the effect is often limited in space and time [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_ritc21_1].
conditionality: The same capture of water that recharges groundwater locally also reduces the water flowing downstream, and several studies measure this as a harm to catchment water yield. In India, a water-balance study estimated that increased rainwater harvesting at watershed scale would cut runoff by about 60% while increasing recharge by only 5% [ev_water_yield_glen12_2], and other analyses there found that even a small share of catchment area under rainwater harvesting sharply reduced the mean runoff coefficient, the share of rainfall converted to streamflow [ev_water_yield_glen09_1]. On China's Loess Plateau, decades of check-dam construction are credited with reducing streamflow by approximately 39% [ev_water_yield_luca21_1]. In Ethiopia, modelling under a high sand-dam development strategy and an extreme climate-change scenario found low-flow months rising from 18.2% of the period to 22.7% and 27.3% in two of those months, and the share of river discharge stored in sand dams in the first rainy season rising to 19.9%, compared with 9.3% under the historical reference period [ev_water_yield_lasa13_4, ev_water_yield_lasa13_5]; under a more moderate strategy with 613 sand dams, the same Ethiopian study found no change in low-flow occurrence [ev_water_yield_lasa13_3]. A separate theoretical modelling study concluded that the impact of rainwater harvesting on watershed water levels may be minimal beyond the immediate vicinity of the structure [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_glen12_8]. Whether a project nets out as a local groundwater gain or a downstream water-yield loss depends on the scale of implementation, a few structures versus watershed-wide development, and on where the account is drawn: the same captured water that recharges a well nearby is water that no longer reaches the river. effect_mechanism: Water harvesting and soil and water conservation reduce food insecurity mainly by raising and steadying harvests and by putting stored water on gardens. In the Brazilian semi-arid, subsurface dams gave families more fruit and vegetables and, by most interviewees' account, more food overall, and production cisterns allow daily irrigation of gardens in households that had not grown or eaten vegetables before [ev_food_security_cirilo03_6, ev_food_security_arsky20_6]; in Burkina Faso, runoff cisterns irrigate small gardens and water livestock, improving food security in the lean season [ev_food_security_roose94_1]. In the field, planting basins (zai pits) raised the odds of a Kenyan plot meeting the household maize requirement to 421.75 against 1.67 in the control, and ground cover raised those odds in Malawi's El Nino season [ev_food_security_boil19_2, ev_food_security_boil19_1]. Household food security rises in proportion to the area of a farm improved with bunds, and beneficiaries of Rwanda's terracing project showed drastically improved food consumption scores against a comparison group [ev_food_security_zoug14_1, ev_food_security_rwa18_5]. WOCAT compilers rate food self-sufficiency as improved and the risk of production failure as lowered, and say why: enough stored water to irrigate during drought in Cambodia, better soil moisture in Ethiopia, more cultivable land and crop diversity in Bhutan, more productive fodder and crops in Burkina Faso, and rehabilitated gullies and farmland in Somalia [ev_food_security_wocat_2844_2017_risk_of_production_failure, ev_food_security_wocat_6715_2023_risk_of_production_failure, ev_food_security_wocat_6891_2023_food_security_selfsufficiency, ev_food_security_wocat_6891_2023_risk_of_production_failure, ev_food_security_wocat_1528_2012_food_security_selfsufficiency, ev_food_security_wocat_1528_2012_risk_of_production_failure, ev_food_security_wocat_7778_2026_food_security_selfsufficiency]. In Ethiopia's Anjene catchment, farmers recalled that before terracing the community was highly food insecure and migrated in search of food even in minor droughts, and that terraces improved crop production and reduced seasonal migration [ev_food_security_adgo13_11]. Ethiopian farmers who adopted rainwater-harvesting irrigation properly improved their dietary status (Desta 2004, cited in a review) [ev_food_security_biaz12_26]. A landscape review of in-situ rainwater harvesting across African drylands rates food security — yields in bad years and the bridging of dry spells — as a benefit with a 'Good' evidence basis [ev_food_security_vohl09_4]. A CILSS regional synthesis adds a further perception survey: in 2005-2006 surveys in Niger, 70 percent of people in villages with natural-resource-management investment reported an improvement in food security, against only 1 percent in control villages [ev_food_security_botreij09_20].

In Brazil, adopters of Embrapa's barraginhas, small semicircular runoff-retention basins, identified food security as the technology's greatest impact, because it guarantees quantity, quality and diversity of food [ev_food_security_mira19_2].
conditionality: Both units say food security improved but neither says by how much: the Ethiopian finding rests on farmer recall and group discussions about the period before and after terracing, and the terraces were maintained for decades with community labour alongside fertiliser use on cereals [ev_food_security_adgo13_11]. The Brazilian finding is an adopter rating in Embrapa's own impact assessment of its technology, not a measured food-security indicator [ev_food_security_mira19_2]. A measured household food-security comparison with untreated farms is needed to state a size.

effect_mechanism: Across mixed soil and water conservation and water-harvesting programmes, the reported route to lower food insecurity is higher yields and irrigated gardens. A review tabulates significantly increased food security from check dams and infiltration pits in Malawi [ev_food_security_ngur26_1]; Brazilian studies judge production-cistern irrigation of small beds feasible and important for household food security [ev_food_security_castro22_3]; and higher yields are cited as improving food security in Burkina Faso, especially on farms with soil and water conservation on over half of their plots [ev_food_security_sawa11h1_5]. A landscape review of rainwater harvesting across African drylands also rates food security — yields in bad years and the bridging of dry spells — as a benefit with a 'Good' evidence basis [ev_food_security_vohl09_4]. A CILSS regional synthesis adds a further perception survey: in 2005-2006 surveys in Niger, 70 percent of people in villages with natural-resource-management investment reported an improvement in food security, against only 1 percent in control villages [ev_food_security_botreij09_20].
conditionality: The size of the gain is limited because the supporting findings are qualitative, cited second-hand and give no size, while the independent evaluations point the other way. In Ethiopia, an impact evaluation of a bundled watershed project found no significant food-security effect for treated households at any participation level [ev_food_security_abate21_4], and public-works participation in communal soil and water investments did not translate into increased food security, possibly because of the short programme [ev_food_security_arega24_1]; both concern mostly off-farm community works. In Niger, families with soil and water conservation produced a surplus of 70 percent in good rainfall years but a deficit of 28 percent in low-rainfall years [ev_food_security_kabo04_1], so benefits may not hold in the dry years that matter most. That rating is the review's own qualitative evaluation across several cited sources, not a single measured contrast [ev_food_security_vohl09_4]. effect_mechanism: In the tropical highlands, soil and water conservation has measured yield gains and measured yield losses, depending on the practice. Gains: an Ethiopian synthesis finds mean grain-yield gains of 322 kg per hectare for stone bunds, 554.3 for tied ridges and 629.2 for mulching, stone and soil bunds raising yields by up to 10% in Tigray, and stone bunds raising soil total nitrogen from 0.16 to 0.20% [ev_crop_yield_adim16_1, ev_crop_yield_adim16_3, ev_crop_yield_adim16_4, ev_crop_yield_adim16_8, ev_soil_nitrogen_adim16_1]; in a Kenyan highland trial, tied ridges in long rains with dry spells gave 4.10 against 3.15 t of maize per hectare with manure and fertiliser, and 2.53 against 1.82 t without inputs (not significant), and tended to give less variable yields [ev_crop_yield_ndun23_3, ev_crop_yield_ndun23_1, ev_yield_stability_ndun23_1]; in Peru, 2 to 4-year old bench terraces gave 20% greater yields than adjacent sloping fields [ev_crop_yield_wei16_4]. In the Ethiopian highlands, fields with long-established fanya juu terraces and grass strips yielded 0.95 against 0.49 t of teff, 1.86 against 0.61 t of barley and 1.73 against 0.77 t of maize per hectare on adjacent un-terraced farms, and the terraces improved the water productivity of the three crops by at least 100% [ev_crop_yield_adgo13_1, ev_crop_yield_adgo13_2, ev_crop_yield_adgo13_3, ev_rain_water_productivity_adgo13_7]. Losses: in the same Ethiopian synthesis fanya juu and soil bunds were associated with yield losses of 54 to 193 kg per hectare, bunds cut yields by up to 7% in the first few years, and annual rainfall above 1000 mm affected performance negatively, which the authors suggest may be waterlogging in the furrows of structures [ev_crop_yield_adim16_2, ev_crop_yield_adim16_7, ev_crop_yield_adim16_6].
conditionality: The class is set by the gains. The fanya juu and soil bund losses and the finding that annual rainfall above 1000 mm affected performance negatively are held out of it, because the synthesis puts that effect down to excessive water availability (water logging) on the furrows of structures [ev_crop_yield_adim16_2, ev_crop_yield_adim16_6]: they are logged as a performance caveat — these structures should not be applied where rainfall is that heavy — rather than as production evidence. The evidence points to three things that separate gains from losses. Practice type: stone bunds, tied ridges and mulching gained, while graded and level fanya juu, soil bunds and grass strips lost yield in the Ethiopian table [ev_crop_yield_adim16_3, ev_crop_yield_adim16_2]. Rainfall: the gaining practices were studied at lower average rainfall (695.1 mm for tied ridges, 876.7 mm for mulching) than the losing bunds (1030.2 to 1454.3 mm), and rainfall above 1000 mm reduced performance [ev_crop_yield_adim16_3, ev_crop_yield_adim16_6]; practice and rainfall travel together in that table, so the two cannot be fully separated. Time: bunds lose yield in the first few years, while the long-established fanya juu terraces of the Ethiopian with-and-without survey yielded more than un-terraced fields, so fanya juu is not a losing practice everywhere [ev_crop_yield_adim16_7, ev_crop_yield_adgo13_1]. Against those terrace gains, the same paper cites Herweg and Ludi (1999) and Kassie et al. (2008) finding that fanya juu, soil and stone bunds and grass strips did not increase crop yield or biomass in the highlands of Ethiopia and Eritrea [ev_crop_yield_adgo13_12]. For a Task Team Leader the actionable reading is to match the structure to the rainfall regime, favouring in-field moisture capture in drier highlands and avoiding fanya juu and soil bunds where waterlogging is likely, and to budget for an early yield dip. At the dry end, tied ridging gave no advantage in the Kenyan short rains with meteorological droughts, since there was little rain to hold [ev_crop_yield_ndun23_2, ev_crop_yield_ndun23_4, ev_crop_yield_ndun23_5]. On quality, both sides rest mainly on the same Ethiopian synthesis of unweighted means pooled across studies; the Kenyan result is a single-site trial whose lower-variability finding was not tested, the Peruvian figure is cited in a review, and the Ethiopian terrace gains are descriptive statistics from a comparison of terraced and adjacent un-terraced farms, not a controlled trial [ev_crop_yield_adim16_1, ev_yield_stability_ndun23_1, ev_crop_yield_wei16_4, ev_crop_yield_adgo13_2].

effect_mechanism: Water-harvesting structures aim to close the rangeland production gap by capturing upslope runoff for planted fodder. In Jordan's Badia, contour furrows and ridges planted with saltbush (Atriplex halimus), a drought-resistant, protein-rich fodder shrub, were reported to harvest more runoff, control soil erosion and considerably improve forage quantity and quality [ev_forage_productivity_stav20_5]. A parallel scheme of micro-catchment water-harvesting bunds in the same Badia, also planted with saltbush, found total soil nitrogen was not significantly different between the bunds and the untreated upslope interspace strip [ev_soil_nitrogen_tats21_2].
conditionality: The forage claim is a review citing two other studies rather than its own measurement, gives no numeric strength for the improvement, and covers the furrow-plus-saltbush combination together, not water harvesting alone [ev_forage_productivity_stav20_5]. The micro-catchment bunds study measured a soil-fertility component rather than forage or yield, found a null result, and could not separate the water-harvesting bund from the planted shrub or the grazing exclusion established alongside it [ev_soil_nitrogen_tats21_2]. With only these two sources — one a qualitative review claim, one a null result — the direction of a rangeland production gain is not firmly established.

effect_mechanism: Pooled across soil and water conservation technologies, large programme evaluations consistently find higher crop yield and production value where farmers have adopted water harvesting. In India, a watershed project raised average rainfed-crop yield by 24% relative to a control group in one phase and by 26% in the next [ev_crop_yield_iegind11_1], and a separate Indian project achieved a 20.8% increase in rainfed-crop productivity attributable to its interventions [ev_crop_yield_utk22_1]. In Ethiopia, early adopters of sustainable land and water management technologies had a 15.2% higher value of production years later [ev_agricultural_production_value_schmidt12_1], and a national impact evaluation found that soil and water conservation on communal land raised crop yields by 9.1% [ev_crop_yield_eth16_1]. In Mauritania, yields in humid watershed zones rose from 0.5 to more than 1.2 tonnes per hectare [ev_crop_yield_mrt14_2]. In Burkina Faso, zaï pits combined with stone lines are credited with sorghum yield increases of over 100%, and maize yield increases of over 100% when the two measures are combined [ev_crop_yield_ngur26_3], and a regional review found soil and water conservation works raising millet yields by 15% to 50% and sorghum yields by 20% to 85% depending on the region, against a considerable decline in cereal yields in control villages [ev_crop_yield_botreij09_1]. A global hydrological model found that expanding rainwater harvesting could raise crop production by 35% at river-basin scale [ev_crop_yield_glen12_9].
conditionality: Some evidence finds harm or no effect, and pooling many technologies together can mask which practice is responsible. A meta-analysis attributed most of its negative-yield observations to in-soil water-harvesting technologies specifically [ev_crop_yield_boum16_2], and in Ethiopia soil and stone bunds reduced crop yield by up to 7% in their first few years after construction [ev_crop_yield_adim16_7]. A separate Ethiopian evaluation found no measurable gain in crop productivity or household income from soil and water conservation promoted mainly for off-farm, community resource protection [ev_crop_yield_abate21_1]. At the extreme end of scale, the same global hydrological model that projected a 35% rise in crop production found this would come with an average 18% reduction in river flows, and a reduction of up to 80% in a single river basin, illustrating the trade-off between on-farm production gains and downstream water availability [ev_crop_yield_glen12_9]. Most of the quantified gains are from low-income countries in the Sahel and East Africa (Burkina Faso, Niger, Ethiopia, Mauritania) and lower-middle-income South Asia (India); the harm and no-effect findings are concentrated in Ethiopia.

effect_mechanism: Semi-circular bunds, Vallerani micro-catchments and half-moons harvest runoff for crops and grasses. On crusted degraded soil in Burkina Faso, 1-m half-moons with compost gave 1372 kg of millet per hectare where direct seeding gave none [ev_crop_yield_zour25h1_2]. A review tabulates crop yield increases of 50–200% from half-moons in Burkina Faso and Niger, and cites micro-basin water harvesting in Zambia doubling maize yields to 3 t per hectare [ev_crop_yield_ngur26_2, ev_crop_yield_ngur26_5]. Negarim micro-catchments with supplementary irrigation supported fruit production at Embrapa Semi-Arid in Brazil, and semi-circular bunds raised millet grain production under African conditions [ev_crop_yield_fao13c_2, ev_crop_yield_fao13c_1]. For the Vallerani System in Burkina Faso the WOCAT compiler reports more fodder in quantity and quality, a surplus of 22–106 grazing days per tropical cattle unit per hectare [ev_livestock_productivity_wocat_1528_2012_animal_production]. A ridge-furrow micro-catchment trial found the single-ridge treatment yielded more on average than no ridging, though not significantly so [ev_crop_yield_wang07_1]. The same synthesis adds two demi-lunes measurements: in Niger's Tahoua region, demi-lunes raised millet yield 78 percent over the Illéla sub-prefecture average [ev_crop_yield_botreij09_15], and in a 2007 dry-spell season on Burkina Faso's Central Plateau, demi-lunes raised grain yield 112 percent, adding at least 800 kilograms of cereal per hectare over the untreated control [ev_crop_yield_botreij09_6].
conditionality: Animal production was rated lower on the Niger sheets because treated rangeland must be protected from grazing for the first years while vegetation establishes [ev_livestock_productivity_wocat_1613_2014_animal_production, ev_livestock_productivity_wocat_1614_2014_animal_production]. The Burkina Faso half-moon contrast is against land where direct seeding produced no grain, with compost added to the pits, so it measures bringing degraded land into production rather than an improvement on a cropped field [ev_crop_yield_zour25h1_2]. The FAO manual cites earlier work, the review figures are ranges and single citations rather than pooled estimates, and the WOCAT units are practitioner judgements [ev_crop_yield_fao13c_1, ev_crop_yield_fao13c_2, ev_crop_yield_ngur26_2, ev_crop_yield_ngur26_5]. Two readings from the same trial pool found no effect: water-use efficiency did not differ significantly between some ridge widths and the control, and in a Jordanian micro-catchment bund system topsoil nitrogen did not differ significantly from the untreated interspace [ev_rain_water_productivity_wang07_4, ev_soil_nitrogen_tats21_2]. Both are project-table or synthesis citations with no significance test reported [ev_crop_yield_botreij09_15, ev_crop_yield_botreij09_6].

In Peru, a benefit of 1.96 soles was found for each sol invested in building cochas [ev_economic_return_card22_1], and modelled bench-terrace gains there could raise per capita incomes by up to 15 percent [ev_household_income_wei16_1].

effect_mechanism: In this semi-arid-AEZ evidence, water harvesting and soil and water conservation mostly raise household income and farm returns, mainly through higher yields, garden irrigation and livestock, though not always. In Zimbabwe, first-year planting-basin farmers earned a maize gross margin of 473.36 US dollars per hectare against 70.60 on conventional plots without fertiliser, and the gain held in the fertilised comparison too [ev_economic_return_mazv09_1, ev_economic_return_mazv09_3]. In Burkina Faso, manual zaï and demi-lunes gave a positive net economic benefit, and groundwater rising behind stone bunds let households earn income from vegetables grown near the wells [ev_economic_return_zoug14_1, ev_economic_return_zour25h1_3, ev_household_income_zoug14_1]. A new study of decentralised irrigation, including rainwater-harvesting ponds, finds household income significantly higher among adopters [ev_household_income_silv26_1]. In Brazil, production cisterns and subsurface dams raised family farm income by about 4.6 percent, rising to nearly 11 percent once the top of the income distribution is excluded, with the clearest gains on the smallest farms, and farmers reported better family income and quality of life from a subsurface dam, though it was not their main income source [ev_household_income_casag22_1, ev_household_income_casag22_2, ev_household_income_brito07_7]. Returns to labour for zaï in Burkina Faso exceed the shadow wage [ev_economic_return_kabo04_1].
conditionality: Against this, a Burkina Faso trial found 30-centimetre zaï running at a net loss against its own investment cost [ev_economic_return_zour25h1_4]; a single soil and water conservation measure did not cover its annual costs [ev_economic_return_zoug14_3]; and Brazil's wider production-cistern programme returned a benefit-cost ratio of 0.0858 over its evaluation window, well below one, with the Brazilian income gain turning negative on farms larger than 10 hectares and two subsurface-dam units finding the income effect almost non-existent or limited in a stagnant local economy [ev_economic_return_casag22_9, ev_household_income_casag22_6, ev_household_income_cirilo03_5, ev_household_income_cirilo03_7]. Income and farm returns are proxies for poverty, most units are farm budgets or household surveys rather than poverty measures, and none follows households over time.

In a Kenyan highland trial, by contrast, net benefits in the short-rains season were higher without tied ridging than with it, except under one soil treatment [ev_economic_return_ndun23_1]. Further farm-budget evidence from mixed crop-livestock systems points the same way. In Zambia, hand-hoe conservation-farming basins gave cotton gross margins 70 percent higher than conventional hand-hoe cultivation and 150 percent higher than conventional ox ploughing, and maize returns to land and peak-season labour 60 to 90 percent higher than hand-hoe tillage [ev_economic_return_hagg03_6, ev_economic_return_hagg03_7, ev_economic_return_hagg03_8]; partial budgets there found a marginal rate of return of 860 percent for switching from hand hoeing to basin digging and 360 percent from ox ploughing to basin digging [ev_economic_return_umar12_2, ev_economic_return_umar12_3]. In the Ethiopian highlands, teff, barley and maize on long-established terraces earned incremental income of US$159, 275 and 141 per hectare per year over un-terraced farms, with an average net present value for barley terracing of US$1542 over 50 years [ev_economic_return_adgo13_4, ev_economic_return_adgo13_5, ev_economic_return_adgo13_6, ev_economic_return_adgo13_10]. In Ethiopia's Tigray, agricultural income from crops and livestock was significantly higher for users than non-users of water-management techniques [ev_household_income_biaz12_18], and Brazilian small family farms saw their monthly income rise once barraginhas filled with water [ev_household_income_mira19_1]. In Kenya's Kitui District, a mixed crop-livestock sand-dam district, calculated household income held up or rose by 27,241 KSh a year for households with a dam against a fall of 38,056 KSh for those without — a difference of 65,297 KSh in a drought year [ev_household_income_pauw08_1].
conditionality: The sides differ in season, in what is compared and in how cleanly water capture is isolated. The Kenyan loss is from a short-rains season of meteorological droughts, in a trial that compares tied ridging with and without under the same soil inputs [ev_economic_return_ndun23_1]; it is the cleanest single comparison here. The Zimbabwean gains set a package of basins, manure, fertiliser and residue against conventional practice, so the water-capture effect is mixed with nutrient supply, and the higher-rainfall figure is a sensitivity scenario with assumed yields [ev_economic_return_mazv09_1, ev_economic_return_mazv09_2]. The Indian figure comes from a farmer survey in which few farms had a pond, the pond water was also used for irrigation, and the compared farms differ in other ways [ev_economic_return_pals23_1]. The evidence therefore cannot say whether water capture alone pays in this farming system; the gains belong to packages, and the one isolated test found a loss in a drought season. All of these are farm budgets rather than measures of household poverty, and none follows households over time [ev_economic_return_mazv09_1, ev_economic_return_mazv09_2, ev_economic_return_mazv09_3, ev_economic_return_ndun23_1, ev_economic_return_pals23_1]. Against this, in Tigray stone-bund building costs about as much each year as the financial benefit from the induced yield gain, roughly breaking even [ev_economic_return_nyss07_10]. The Zambian and Ethiopian gains are farm budgets, and the Ethiopian terrace income excludes family labour and is measured on terraces maintained for decades, so it shows what an established, well-maintained system returns rather than the first years after building [ev_economic_return_hagg03_6, ev_economic_return_adgo13_4]. effect_mechanism: Zai pits, planting pits, contour bunds and planting basins can raise farm income by raising yields. Returns to labour for these practices in Burkina Faso exceed the shadow wage, and bunds show returns above cost at subproject level in Mauritania [ev_economic_return_kabo04_1, ev_economic_return_mrt14_5]. In Zimbabwe, first-year planting-basin farmers earned a maize gross margin of 473.36 USD per hectare against 70.60 on conventional plots in the low-rainfall budget, with 866.84 against 357.16 for experienced farmers in high rainfall [ev_economic_return_mazv09_1, ev_economic_return_mazv09_2]. Zambian crop budgets give hand-hoe conservation-farming basins returns per hectare 70 percent higher than conventional hand hoe cultivation and 150 percent higher than conventional plowing for cotton, and returns to land and peak-season labor 60 to 90 percent higher than hand hoe tillage for maize [ev_economic_return_hagg03_6, ev_economic_return_hagg03_7, ev_economic_return_hagg03_8]. In Zambia, partial budgets found it profitable for a household to switch to conservation agriculture, with a marginal rate of return of 860% from hand hoeing to basin digging and 360% from ploughing to basin digging [ev_economic_return_umar12_2, ev_economic_return_umar12_3]. In Mozambique basins returned $148 per hectare against $104 under conventional tillage, an imputed value of $44 per hectare for a risk-neutral farmer [ev_economic_return_kida19_2, ev_economic_return_kida19_4]. In Ghana tied ridges with grass strips gave a higher net return than flat-land maize in 2010 despite a slightly higher cost [ev_economic_return_dalt14_3], and in Nigeria wood-shavings mulch on a flat bed was expected to increase the financial benefits to farmers by 238% [ev_economic_return_chir06_11]. Further figures from the same CILSS Sahel synthesis: in Niger, the internal rate of return on zaï pits was 82 percent where the farmer rehabilitated land he already owned, falling to 39 percent where he bought degraded land to rehabilitate, still a quick payback [ev_economic_return_botreij09_26]; on Burkina Faso's Central Plateau, zaï planting pits returned an internal rate of 93 percent [ev_economic_return_botreij09_32].
conditionality: The evidence conflicts, and what pulls it apart is how the gain is valued and against what. Crop budgets built on bundled input packages put basins well ahead [ev_economic_return_hagg03_6, ev_economic_return_hagg03_8, ev_economic_return_mazv09_1]; but a Zimbabwe household panel that values predicted yields with inputs held constant finds conservation agriculture generates less revenue than traditional cultivation over a large portion of the rainfall distribution [ev_economic_return_mich19_8]. Other losses are season- or practice-specific: tied ridging in a Kenyan drought season, where net benefits were higher without it, and 30-cm zaï on a Burkina Faso trial, which ran at a loss of −98 624 FCFA per hectare against the experiment's own investment cost [ev_economic_return_ndun23_1, ev_economic_return_zour25h1_4]. Manual zai gives far smaller net benefits than mechanised zai [ev_economic_return_zoug14_1]. The Zimbabwe margins include manure and fertiliser and the high-rainfall figure is a sensitivity scenario [ev_economic_return_mazv09_2]; the Zambian returns are bundled with early planting and purchased inputs, which the authors say dominate the maize results [ev_economic_return_hagg03_8]; and the Zimbabwe panel figure is gross revenue with labour unvalued, so it is neither a profit nor a poverty measure [ev_economic_return_mich19_8]. The newer field trials split the same way, and cost is what separates them: in Nigeria the high production costs of open and tied ridging, with or without mulch, gave net economic losses of about 1, 0.5, 11 and 12%, while mulch on the flat bed paid [ev_economic_return_chir06_10, ev_economic_return_chir06_11]; and in Mozambique basin and conventional returns did not differ significantly at intermediate elevation [ev_economic_return_kida19_3]. The Zambian rates of return come from partial budgets of a single crop, maize. Farm income and returns are proxies for poverty. effect_mechanism: Small reservoirs, sand dams, farm ponds, runoff cisterns and subsurface dams provide water for dry-season irrigation of vegetables and fruit and for livestock, shifting cropping towards higher-value crops and raising household income [ev_household_income_veno12_2, ev_household_income_ritc21_3]. In Kenya, farmers living near sand dams saw average income rise by 60% as more water in dry periods raised farm yields [ev_household_income_lasage08_1]. In the same Kitui, Kenya sand-dam district, a separate household survey found calculated income held up or rose by 27,241 KSh a year for dam households against a fall of 38,056 KSh for those without — a difference of 65,297 KSh in a drought year [ev_household_income_pauw08_1]. Reviews add that rainwater-harvesting ponds brought statistically significant gains in household income in Burkina Faso, water storage gave Ethiopian smallholders greater income security, harvested water used with precision irrigation in Ethiopia reached a net water value of up to 1.53 USD per cubic metre, and benefit-cost ratios reached up to 3.38 with payback periods of 6.8 to 12 years; Indian farms with a farm pond reported net returns of 857 USD per hectare against 586 without [ev_household_income_silv26_1, ev_household_income_silv26_2, ev_economic_return_silv26_1, ev_economic_return_silv26_2, ev_economic_return_pals23_1]. In Brazil, an Embrapa survey of some communities found small-farm incomes rose by about half a minimum wage per month after the second filling of the barraginhas [ev_household_income_mira19_1]. The Cambodian pond compiler rates farm income up because every crop yielded well once there was enough irrigation water [ev_household_income_wocat_2844_2017_farm_income]. Returns on stored runoff can be high: farm-pond supplemental irrigation of maize in Kenya gave net seasonal revenue of US$ 150 and could raise the annual return by 150% (Ngigi et al. 2005), road-catchment harvesting for paddy in Tanzania returned more than US$ 12 per person-day against US$ 3.7 for rainfed sorghum (Hatibu et al. 2006), and a Peruvian programme building 31 cochas returned 1.96 soles per sol invested (Tafur, cited in a programme review) [ev_economic_return_biaz12_20, ev_economic_return_biaz12_21, ev_economic_return_card22_1]. A Burkina Faso and Kenya model puts net profit from water harvesting with supplemental irrigation, fertiliser and an off-season tomato crop at 151–626 USD per hectare a year in Burkina Faso and 109–477 in Kenya, against at most 15 and 40–130 under current practice [ev_economic_return_fox05_3, ev_economic_return_fox05_4]. In Pakistan, maize irrigated from harvested rainwater earned 0.28 US$ net per cubic metre in the first year, with a cumulative benefit-cost ratio projected at 2.02 by the second year and 3.53 by the third, and fish farming in a farm pond earned US$ 1799 net on average, about US$ 2951 in mini-dams [ev_economic_return_waqa25_5, ev_household_income_waqa25_7]. In Rajasthan, India, modelled recharge from check dams was estimated sufficient to irrigate part of the winter crop area and judged responsible for 16 percent of farm income [ev_household_income_dash17_3].
conditionality: Most literature magnitudes are secondary citations in reviews or vote counts [ev_household_income_saru19_3, ev_household_income_veno12_3]. Sand dams are judged likely not cost-efficient for water supply, Brazilian subsurface dams produced little cash income where electricity, investment capital or an irrigation tradition were missing, and the high Brazilian benefit-cost ratios come from an upper-middle-income context [ev_economic_return_ritc21_1, ev_household_income_cirilo03_7, ev_economic_return_cirilo03_10]. The Kenyan sand-dam income rise compares a small sample of households with a control catchment [ev_household_income_lasage08_1]; the reviewed figures are reported at their upper end, the Indian pond returns come from a cross-sectional survey confounded by farm size and assets [ev_economic_return_silv26_2, ev_economic_return_pals23_1], and the barraginha income finding is Embrapa's self-assessment of its own technology from an informal survey [ev_household_income_mira19_1]. Income and returns are proxies for poverty. The returns hinge on what the water is used for and on inputs: in the Burkina Faso model the yield gain from supplemental irrigation alone does not compensate for the labour and capital invested [ev_economic_return_fox05_2], and in Pakistan pearl millet irrigated from harvested rainwater lost 0.27 US$ per cubic metre in the first year and stayed below break-even by the third [ev_economic_return_waqa25_6]. The Kenyan, Tanzanian and Peruvian returns are second-hand citations, the model profits rely on a high-value tomato crop and vary with the cost put on labour, and the Pakistani figures are projections assuming constant prices and water productivity [ev_economic_return_biaz12_20, ev_economic_return_card22_1, ev_economic_return_fox05_3, ev_economic_return_waqa25_5]. That figure is a calculation from estimated irrigable area rather than a measured income contrast, and is bundled with the well-pumping the recharge supplies [ev_household_income_dash17_3]. In a separate Ethiopian sand-dam catchment, a household survey found no clear difference in economic situation between households with and without dam access, though the authors attribute the weak contrast partly to the small number of dam-linked households surveyed [ev_household_income_lasa13_2]. The Kitui income comparison is a cross-sectional household survey with multi-year recall rather than a randomised comparison; dams were not placed at random, and dam households also applied more terracing, bunds and grass lines whose effect cannot be separated from the dam's own [ev_household_income_pauw08_1].

effect_mechanism: In the Maghreb, contour structures have been reported both to hold runoff and to accelerate erosion. Staggered earth bunds (tabia) in Morocco store the runoff of all rains below 50 mm on the field [ev_runoff_reduction_roos10_1]. In Algeria, a poorly maintained banquette becomes a factor accelerating erosion, because the smallest unrepaired breach triggers a chain reaction through the whole network in torrential and prolonged rains [ev_erosion_hazard_arab04_2].
conditionality: Two conditions separate the sides in the sources. Maintenance: the acceleration is tied explicitly to unrepaired breaches in state-built banquettes [ev_erosion_hazard_arab04_2]. Storm size: the tabia hold runoff only up to rains of 50 mm, and in bigger storms the excess overtops them and gullies the whole slope [ev_runoff_reduction_roos10_1]. The actionable reading is to plan and fund upkeep and spillways, not only construction. Elsewhere banquettes simply did not stop gullying: gullied areas on Tunisian banquette land grew by 12% between 1963 and 1973, and over 1947-1968 Algerian banquettes had no influence on the sedimentation rate of the Oued Fodda dam [ev_erosion_hazard_arab04_1, ev_sediment_retention_arab04_1]. Neither side is measured on plots: the protective statement is from an expert manual and the harmful ones are secondary citations within a national evaluation, and the two concern different structures, tabia and banquettes [ev_runoff_reduction_roos10_1, ev_erosion_hazard_arab04_2].

effect_mechanism: Physical SWC works under public-works and watershed programmes reduce soil loss and downstream runoff, and sediment-control dams with terraces and vegetation trap sediment in the catchment. A meta-analysis of traditional in-situ water harvesting finds soil loss cut by 58.66% and runoff by 53% on average, with soil and stone bunds reducing soil loss by 55.06% and runoff by 49.2% [ev_erosion_hazard_tefe24_1, ev_runoff_reduction_tefe24_1, ev_erosion_hazard_tefe24_4, ev_runoff_reduction_tefe24_5]; in Ethiopian catchments, stone bunds, check dams and vegetation regrowth cut sediment yield from 8.5 to 1.9 t per hectare a year [ev_erosion_hazard_meko14_1, ev_erosion_hazard_meko14_2]. Ethiopian catchment studies cited in a review report physical soil and water conservation decreasing runoff by up to 88% (Taye et al., 2015; Haregeweyn et al., 2015), and integrated catchment management at May Zeg Zeg cutting surface runoff volume by 81% (Nyssen et al., 2010) [ev_runoff_reduction_gebr18_7, ev_runoff_reduction_gebr18_8].
conditionality: Nearly all units are programme or lender reports from Ethiopia, India and China, often perception surveys or before/after comparisons; an Uttarakhand water budget showed surface runoff slightly increasing, the Karnataka runoff comparison is against another SWC programme, and IEG doubts the India runoff measurements. Effects mixing runoff and soil-loss metrics are only components of erosion risk. A catchment-restoration meta-analysis in Ethiopia finds minimal effect of catchment treatment on runoff in drought-prone areas with annual rainfall below 500 mm [ev_runoff_reduction_meaza22_3]. The Ethiopian catchment results combine structures with grazing control and vegetation regeneration and are cited in a review, so the share due to the works is not isolated [ev_erosion_hazard_meko14_1]. The 88% and 81% runoff figures are cited second-hand: the first is an upper bound, and the second is a before-and-after result for a catchment-management package rather than the structures alone [ev_runoff_reduction_gebr18_7, ev_runoff_reduction_gebr18_8].

effect_mechanism: Terracing and retaining walls hold soil on slopes, which an evaluation in Morocco expects to reduce siltation of downstream rivers and dam storage [ev_sediment_retention_iegmar09_3]. Reviews add that fanya juu trapped 64% of sediment (80% with vetiver grass), and bench terracing cut sediment yield by 58% in a small USA watershed [ev_sediment_retention_meko14_6, ev_sediment_retention_meko14_5]. A terracing review finds terraces reasonably effective at reducing sediment transport, though about 20%–30% of sediment may still be delivered [ev_sediment_retention_arna15_6]. On Tigray cropland, Gebremichael and colleagues measured eroded soil accumulating behind stone bunds at 59 t per hectare a year across 202 plots, and a later paper by the same team reports, citing Nigussie et al. (2005), strongly decreased specific sediment yield in reservoirs whose catchments have a high density of stone bunds [ev_sediment_retention_gebr05_2, ev_sediment_retention_nyss07_13].
conditionality: The Morocco unit is an evaluator assertion; nothing on water chemistry is measured, and siltation is a component proxy [ev_sediment_retention_iegmar09_3]. The added sediment figures are secondary citations in reviews, in extreme rainfall the sediment accumulated on terraces can reach the channel [ev_sediment_retention_arna15_6], the bench-terrace figure comes from a high-income watershed, and Algerian banquettes had no influence on the sedimentation rate of a downstream dam over 1947-1968 [ev_sediment_retention_meko14_5, ev_sediment_retention_arab04_1]. The Tigray figure is on-field trapping, a component proxy for downstream water quality, part of it soil moved by tillage rather than by water, and the reservoir finding is a second-hand citation without a stated size; both come from the same research team [ev_sediment_retention_gebr05_2, ev_sediment_retention_nyss07_13].

effect_mechanism: Storage and recharge structures ease water stress in semi-arid areas: production cisterns in semi-arid Brazil keep livestock watered while clay tanks are dry, an agency review credits consumption and production cisterns with a large drop in rural establishments without any water source, and subsurface dams raise water levels in existing wells used when other sources dry up [ev_water_access_deficit_arsky20_5, ev_water_access_deficit_castro22_1, ev_water_access_deficit_cirilo03_1]. In the field, pits and furrows keep rain in the root zone: in Burkina Faso zaï of 30–40 cm diameter and 1-m half-moons retained moisture for 2-3 weeks through dry spells, and zaï can retain moisture in the soil for seven to ten days after rainfall; in semi-arid Brazil tied furrows kept more soil moisture than the traditional flat system at all crop stages and depths [ev_soil_water_retention_zour25h1_7, ev_soil_water_retention_sawa11h1_8, ev_soil_water_retention_brito07_9].
conditionality: Supply is bounded by storage: 57% of Kenyan sand dams would hold 4 months of water for their reported beneficiaries [ev_water_access_deficit_neuf17_1]. The Brazilian units are implementer or agency assessments, interviews or census inference from an upper-middle-income context rather than the low-income target [ev_water_access_deficit_castro22_1, ev_water_access_deficit_arsky20_5]. Well-level evidence for semi-arid bunds and zaï now sits in the catchment water yield rows. What upstream capture does to water downstream is a separate question, answered in the catchment water yield rows. The zaï and half-moon results come with compost in the pits, so the moisture gain cannot be credited to the pit alone [ev_soil_water_retention_zour25h1_7, ev_soil_water_retention_sawa11h1_8]. In the Brazilian trial deep ploughing, which is tillage alone and not a capture structure, scored as high as the tied furrows, and the trial ran a single season at a station of the agency that promotes the technology [ev_soil_water_retention_brito07_9].

effect_mechanism: Water-harvesting bunds and furrows raise soil moisture in rangeland by concentrating upslope runoff onto the treated strip. In Iran's Sistan-Baluchistan province, contour furrows 20-25 cm deep were reported to increase soil moisture and boost the productivity of the shrub vegetation they were cut for [ev_soil_moisture_stav20_6]. In Jordan's Badia, gravimetric soil moisture measured in micro-catchment water-harvesting bunds was 20.1 percent against 12.1 percent in the untreated interspace upslope [ev_soil_moisture_tats21_1].
conditionality: The Iranian finding is a review's citation of another study rather than a direct measurement, with the increase not quantified [ev_soil_moisture_stav20_6]. The Jordanian figure is a single sampling date at the peak of the rainy season, compares the bund to the runoff-contributing interspace strip (not to unworked land away from the system), and the water-harvesting bund was built together with planted saltbush shrubs and a grazing exclusion, so the moisture gain cannot be separated from those [ev_soil_moisture_tats21_1]. Both cases are upper-middle-income dryland pastoral settings; direct evidence for lower-income rangeland systems is not yet available.

effect_mechanism: Watershed treatment reduces reliance on outside supply: participating villages in India saw reduced water transportation by tanker compared with nonparticipating villages [ev_water_access_deficit_verm19_1], and an agency review credits consumption and production cisterns in semi-arid Brazil with a significant contribution to wider access to water [ev_water_access_deficit_castro22_1]. In India, discharge of springs and streams rose in treated watersheds: a sample study in Himachal Pradesh reports a 40 percent increase in water discharge in spring and stream sources [ev_water_regulation_hp17_1], and the Uttarakhand project achieved an average 21 percent increase in water discharge from perennial water sources in sampled micro-watersheds, against a target of 25 percent [ev_water_regulation_utk22_6]. Measured soil moisture adds a field route: a meta-analysis of in-situ practices finds they improve soil moisture retention by 59%, with soil/stone bunds at an SMD of 76.4% [ev_soil_water_retention_tefe24_1, ev_soil_water_retention_tefe24_3]; in Burkina Faso zaï of 30–40 cm diameter and 1-m half-moons retained moisture for 2-3 weeks through dry spells [ev_soil_water_retention_zour25h1_7]; and Indian project watersheds showed an increase in soil moisture content by 30.5 percent compared to the IWMP sites [ev_soil_water_retention_kar20_2]. Water productivity, the grain produced per unit of rain, is a route by which capture eases water stress. The water-productivity evidence points the same way: FAO compilers list improved water use efficiency among the main benefits of rainwater harvesting, the WOCAT guideline authors find that all water harvesting groups indicate improved water use efficiency, mostly high to medium, through reduced evaporation loss and better soil water availability, and a review sentence, citing earlier work, says capture approaches often lead also to higher water productivity because denser canopies shade the soil [ev_rain_water_productivity_faoslm11_1, ev_rain_water_productivity_wocwh13_1, ev_rain_water_productivity_rock10_1]. A terracing meta-analysis across China also enters here: soil moisture on terraced land was significantly higher on average by 12.4 percent relative to sloping land, with the largest improvement on grassland terraces (28.2 percent) and benefits 28.6 percent higher in semi-humid areas than in semi-arid or humid areas [ev_soil_moisture_chen20_1, ev_soil_moisture_chen20_8, ev_soil_moisture_chen20_9, ev_soil_moisture_chen20_10, ev_soil_moisture_chen20_11, ev_soil_moisture_chen20_12]. A CILSS regional synthesis adds a further recharge observation: in Burkina Faso's Oula department, 21 of 23 villages reported that wells which used to dry up every February and March now hold water year-round since the works were built, which villagers attributed to better recharge of the water table [ev_water_access_deficit_botreij09_19].
conditionality: The tanker reduction is a reported programme assessment [ev_water_access_deficit_verm19_1], and the Brazilian unit is an agency inference from census figures in an upper-middle-income context [ev_water_access_deficit_castro22_1]. The Indian spring and stream discharge figures come from World Bank completion reports, the lender's own evaluation, measured before and after without untreated comparison sites, for catchment treatment that bundles plantations, trenches, ponds and check dams with water-harvesting structures, so the gain cannot be credited to water harvesting alone [ev_water_regulation_hp17_1, ev_water_regulation_utk22_6]. Groundwater-recharge evidence, with its limits, now sits in the catchment water yield rows, which also answer what upstream capture does to water downstream. The pooled 59% covers mixed in-situ practices, and the zaï and half-moon result comes with compost in the pits, so neither credits a single structure [ev_soil_water_retention_tefe24_1, ev_soil_water_retention_zour25h1_7]. The Indian soil-moisture comparison is a project-commissioned study of a package of soil and water conservation structures [ev_soil_water_retention_kar20_2]. These are compiler and author judgements across groups, direction only, and the review sentence is second-hand; the WOCAT authors also note that some case studies indicate little to no improvement in water use efficiency [ev_rain_water_productivity_faoslm11_1, ev_rain_water_productivity_wocwh13_1, ev_rain_water_productivity_rock10_1]. The same meta-analysis found the benefit reversed to a deficit at depths of 140-160 cm and 180-200 cm, with a considerable benefit only at 40-60 cm, and the benefit below a 15-degree slope was not significant [ev_soil_moisture_chen20_13, ev_soil_moisture_chen20_14]. It is a cross-site meta-analysis, not a single measured contrast. That is the villagers' own attribution across a set of villages rather than a measurement against a comparable untreated well [ev_water_access_deficit_botreij09_19].

effect_mechanism: Pits, basins, bunds and tied ridges catch rain where it falls and hold it in the root zone. A meta-analysis finds infiltration pits have the highest SMD of 114.4% for soil moisture retention, with tied ridging at 48.9% [ev_soil_water_retention_tefe24_2, ev_soil_water_retention_tefe24_5]. In Burkina Faso zaï can retain moisture in the soil for seven to ten days after rainfall [ev_soil_water_retention_sawa11h1_8]; in Brazil tied furrows kept more soil moisture than the traditional flat system at all crop stages and depths [ev_soil_water_retention_brito07_9]; and in Ethiopia hand-dug planting basins held more topsoil water than unmulched plots at Ziway at flowering (27.4 against 25.5) and at maturity (26.5 against 25.9) [ev_soil_water_retention_sime15h2_4, ev_soil_water_retention_sime15h2_6]. Mulching, the soil-cover form of in-situ water harvesting, improves soil moisture retention with an SMD of 54.0% in the meta-analysis, and maize-stalk mulch in Ethiopia held more topsoil water than unmulched plots at Ziway at each stage measured [ev_soil_water_retention_tefe24_4, ev_soil_water_retention_sime15h2_1, ev_soil_water_retention_sime15h2_3, ev_soil_water_retention_sime15h2_5]. Water productivity, the grain produced per unit of rain, is a route by which capture eases water stress. Grain per unit of rain rises with capture in a set of East and Southern African trials: the best conservation-farming practice per site gave yield increases ranging from 20 to 120% over conventional tillage whilst rain water productivity improved with 10–50% [ev_rain_water_productivity_rock09_1]. In an on-farm trial at Houndé, Burkina Faso, stone rows with zaï pits, every arm also receiving manure, lifted maize rain water productivity from 3.10 kg per hectare per mm under the farmers' practice of oxen ploughing with NPK and urea to 6.61 [ev_rain_water_productivity_koro17_1]. A review reports that contour tied-ridging in eastern Sudan gave the highest water use efficiency of the treatments compared [ev_rain_water_productivity_ngur26_3]. In a Nigerian field trial, tied ridging with wood-shavings mulch stored 8, 26 and 14.4% more soil water than the flat bed in successive seasons, and raised rainfall water use efficiency of sorghum grain from 1.26 to 1.97 kg per hectare per mm [ev_soil_moisture_chir06_7, ev_rain_water_productivity_chir06_9]. Reviews cite tied ridging, open ridging and sub-soiling improving root-zone soil water by 24%, 15% and 3% over traditional tillage in drought-stricken Wollo, Ethiopia (McHugh et al., 2007), tied ridges cutting surface runoff by about 60% and raising rooting-zone soil water by at least 13% in northern Ethiopia (Araya and Stroosnijder, 2010), and 20–25 cm deep contour furrows increasing soil moisture and shrub productivity on rangeland in Iran's Sistan Baluchistan (Jahantigh and Pessarakli, 2009) [ev_soil_moisture_biaz12_6, ev_soil_moisture_dile13_1, ev_soil_moisture_biaz12_8, ev_soil_moisture_stav20_6]. In a Zimbabwean on-farm trial, dead-level contour ridges on silt loam held significantly more soil moisture than an adjacent plot without ridges shortly after a 60 mm rainfall day (14 against 12.1 mm) and after a dry spell lasting 3 weeks (10.4 against 9.2 mm) [ev_soil_moisture_mhiz13_1, ev_soil_moisture_mhiz13_2]. The Chinese terracing meta-analysis confirms soil-water-storage effectiveness across all six terrace types studied [ev_soil_moisture_chen20_2].
conditionality: Tillage alone is not water harvesting: in the Brazilian trial deep ploughing, a tillage practice, scored as high as the tied furrows [ev_soil_water_retention_brito07_9]. The Brazilian trial ran a single season at a station of the agency that promotes the technology [ev_soil_water_retention_brito07_9]. At Melkassa the Ethiopian mulch plots differed from unmulched plots only at maturity, not at planting or flowering [ev_soil_water_retention_sime15h2_7, ev_soil_water_retention_sime15h2_9, ev_soil_water_retention_sime15h2_11]. The Ethiopian basins did not differ from unmulched plots at planting at Ziway or at any stage at Melkassa [ev_soil_water_retention_sime15h2_2, ev_soil_water_retention_sime15h2_8, ev_soil_water_retention_sime15h2_10, ev_soil_water_retention_sime15h2_12]. Under meteorological drought and dry spells in Kenya, tied ridging without organic inputs was insufficient in soil moisture conservation since there was little or no rainwater to be held in the basins [ev_soil_water_retention_ndun23_1]. A review found no significant effect of infiltration trenches on soil moisture because only four studies provided sufficient statistical data [ev_soil_water_retention_locat20_1]. The zaï result comes with compost in the pits [ev_soil_water_retention_sawa11h1_8]. The Mauritanian well-level and Andean trench evidence now sits in the in-situ catchment water yield row, which also answers what upstream capture does to water downstream. Those best-practice arms are bundled: planting pits, basins or ripper-with-ridging (the capture element, which is the practice here) come with reduced tillage and mostly with fertiliser, and tillage alone is not water harvesting [ev_rain_water_productivity_rock09_1]. The trial-level readings are weaker: the authors find no clear tillage effect on rain water productivity in Kenya, no clear effects of tillage in Ethiopia (where the gains that do show come with fertilised treatments), and only a tendency of improvement in semi-arid Tanzania [ev_rain_water_productivity_rock09_3, ev_rain_water_productivity_rock09_5, ev_rain_water_productivity_rock09_4]. The Burkina Faso trial covers a single season, and every conservation arm also received manure, so its gain belongs to the package rather than to the structures alone [ev_rain_water_productivity_koro17_1]. At Houndé, grass strips with zaï (4.84 against 3.10) were not significantly different from the control, and at Péni neither grass strips with zaï (4.51) nor earth bunds with contour ploughing (4.31) differed significantly from the control (3.53), the authors stating that water was not limiting at Péni, which had more rain than Houndé that season [ev_rain_water_productivity_koro17_2, ev_rain_water_productivity_koro17_3, ev_rain_water_productivity_koro17_4]. The Sudan comparison ranks treatments without a no-practice value [ev_rain_water_productivity_ngur26_3]. In the Nigerian trial, open and tied ridging without mulch stored only a few per cent more soil water, significant on only one out of the nine measurement dates, and did not consistently raise water use efficiency, so ridging may not be an improvement without a residue mulch [ev_soil_moisture_chir06_7, ev_rain_water_productivity_chir06_8]. The Ethiopian and Iranian soil-moisture figures are cited second-hand. On the sandy field of the same Zimbabwe trial, where little runoff was generated, the ridges made no significant difference to soil moisture after heavy rain or after the dry spell [ev_soil_moisture_mhiz13_3]. That is a meta-analysis finding for terracing structures specifically, not an in-situ-family measurement [ev_soil_moisture_chen20_2].

effect_mechanism: Terraces and stone lines capture and retain rainwater on slopes, and stone lines contribute to increased infiltration of rainwater into the soil, thereby replenishing water resources [ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_6610_2022_water_quantity, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_6610_2022_water_availability]. Measured soil moisture supports this: a meta-analysis gives terraces an SMD of 40.5% for soil moisture retention [ev_soil_water_retention_tefe24_6], a global terracing synthesis finds terraced sites more efficient than slopes at conserving soil water, with a mean δsm of 1.2 [ev_soil_water_retention_wei16_1], and conversion of slopeland to leveled fields in China increased moisture retention [ev_soil_water_retention_iegchn07_2]. Water productivity, the grain produced per unit of rain, is a route by which capture eases water stress. The FAO compilers rate improving water productivity for the cross-slope barrier group at the middle mark of their scale [ev_rain_water_productivity_faoslm11_3]. In Ethiopia's Anjene catchment, terraces improved the water productivity of teff, barley and maize by at least 100% against un-terraced plots [ev_rain_water_productivity_adgo13_7]. A review of farming terraces notes that the soil stays humid for longer on terraces than on sloping fields, and that a very flat terrace bed lets rain pond, reducing runoff and increasing infiltration [ev_soil_moisture_arna15_7]. In Tigray, stone bunds enhance soil moisture storage on both sides of the bund, especially on loamy and sandy soils, with 0.05–0.1 g g−1 more soil moisture at 1–1.5 m depth persisting for at least 2 months after the rainy season (Vancampenhout, 2003, reported by Nyssen et al.) [ev_soil_moisture_nyss07_4]. In Peru, farmers say the soil on bench terraces remains humid twice as long as on sloping fields [ev_soil_moisture_post05_8]. The Chinese terracing meta-analysis adds further terrace types confirmed effective for soil water storage [ev_soil_moisture_chen20_3, ev_soil_moisture_chen20_4, ev_soil_moisture_chen20_5, ev_soil_moisture_chen20_6], and in a Canadian potato belt simulated soil moisture was significantly higher on terraced than non-terraced fields [ev_soil_moisture_lian19_4].
conditionality: The Tunisian stone-line units are practitioner judgements, and catchment modelling in Peru found no difference in crop water distribution with partial terracing [ev_water_regulation_willem21_1]. Abandoned or degraded terraces worsen water regulation [ev_water_regulation_willem21_2]. The recharge estimates for terraces and contour ridges now sit in the terracing catchment water yield row. The terracing ratio is an unweighted mean across extracted cases from mixed-income countries [ev_soil_water_retention_wei16_1], and the Chinese finding comes from an independent World Bank evaluation reporting project monitoring with no control [ev_soil_water_retention_iegchn07_2]. That is a compiler judgement for a group spanning earth bunds, stone lines, vegetative strips and fanya juu terraces, direction only [ev_rain_water_productivity_faoslm11_3]. The same review cites work finding that the infiltration capacity of the soil is not particularly affected by terracing (Posthumus and Stroosnijder, 2010), so the gain comes from water held longer on the flat bed rather than a change in the soil [ev_soil_moisture_arna15_7]. The Anjene figure compares long-maintained terraces with un-terraced plots at a single catchment where farmers also use fertiliser [ev_rain_water_productivity_adgo13_7]. The Peruvian humidity finding is the farmers' account; the study could not measure it [ev_soil_moisture_post05_8]. The Tigray soil-moisture figure is an earlier study reported within Nyssen et al. [ev_soil_moisture_nyss07_4]. The Canadian comparison is modelled rather than measured and the terrace system was built together with grassed waterways, so the moisture gain cannot be separated from those [ev_soil_moisture_lian19_4].
